FEEDBACK-GATED MODULATION SUPPORTS VISUAL NAVIGATION

Jingcheng Shi

GitHub

We compare EmbCLIP with EmbCLIP-GaWF on unseen RoboTHOR environments. Both agents receive RGB images and a target object category.

Method

We retain EmbCLIP’s frozen CLIP visual encoder and goal-conditioned processing, and replace its GRU with a parameter-matched GaWF module. The previous step’s detached policy logits feed GaWF’s gates, which modulate its input and recurrent weights.

Results

I. EmbCLIP-GaWF Performs Better Under Lightweight Training

With lightweight 5M-step training (about 2.5% of EmbCLIP’s original 200M-step budget), EmbCLIP-GaWF achieves higher overall success rate (SR) and success weighted by path length (SPL) than equally trained EmbCLIP.

We compare success rate (SR), success weighted by path length (SPL), and success weighted by episode length (SEL). SEL follows the metric introduced by EmbCLIP-Codebook.

II. Recurrent Feedback Guides Navigation Toward the Object Goal

Under lightweight training, EmbCLIP-GaWF achieves a higher overall success rate. The paired videos highlight its advantages on selected navigation tasks.

In these selected cases, EmbCLIP-GaWF reaches the object goal with fewer actions than EmbCLIP.

III. EmbCLIP-GaWF Encodes Important Task-Relevant Information

We use Grad-CAM to examine the visual cues associated with stopping after Object Goal Navigation training. The selected successful views illustrate object-goal sensitivity in the model with top-down feedback, alongside responses to surrounding objects and other visual cues in EmbCLIP.

These selected maps illustrate how top-down feedback can emphasize object-goal cues over surrounding distractions also present in the EmbCLIP baseline. Warm regions indicate positive sensitivity of the stopping decision.
